findings.note: internal/fsm/run/store_jsonl.go:186-193 - readRaw loops on f.Read and breaks on ANY non-nil error, discarding it and returning the partial buffer with err == nil. A mid-file I/O error (EIO, a network filesystem hiccup, the exact class of failure the rest of this store defends against with fsync, O_NOFOLLOW and torn sidecars) therefore looks identical to a short file. splitLines (internal/fsm/run/store.go:112) then reports the truncated final line as a TornTail, prepareAppend rejects the append with ERR_AUDIT_TORN, and the documented recovery, RepairTail (store_jsonl.go:243-259), calls truncateTo(auditPath, torn.Offset) - permanently destroying the healthy tail of a durable audit log. The chain hash cannot detect this because the partial prefix verifies cleanly. Use io.ReadAll (or return rerr unless errors.Is(rerr, io.EOF)) so a read error surfaces as ERR_STORE_PATH. Note the inconsistency: this same PR adds internal/state/state_test.go specifically to prove Close errors are not swallowed, and internal/state/state.go:24 shows the project already uses a test seam when an error branch is otherwise hard to cover.

findings.note: internal/fsm/run/store_jsonl.go:346-355 - the lock descriptor leaks when syscall.Flock fails with anything other than EWOULDBLOCK (ENOLCK, EINTR, EBADF). The EWOULDBLOCK branch closes f, but the generic `if err != nil { return nil, pathErr(0, err) }` branch does not, so a long-lived process that retries Lock accumulates open descriptors. Close f before returning in that branch.

evidence.note: return nil, pathErr(0, err) with f still open when flock failed for a non-EWOULDBLOCK reason

findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:82-89 - MaxFileBytes is documented as a cap because 'the peek reads it before the run is verified', but os.ReadFile completes first and the length check runs on the already-resident buffer. The cap therefore bounds what is parsed, not what is allocated: a multi-gigabyte judge.yaml is read into memory in full before being rejected. Stat the file, or read through an io.LimitReader of MaxFileBytes+1, to make the cap do what its comment claims.

findings.note: internal/fsm/mockai/mockai.go:91 - yaml.NewDecoder(strings.NewReader(string(raw))) makes a full second copy of the file bytes for no reason; bytes.NewReader(raw) is equivalent and allocation-free. Related: the decoder consumes only the first YAML document, so a second '---' document in judge.yaml is silently ignored despite KnownFields(true) otherwise enforcing strictness.
